audit_mode: read-only source and test implementation inspection; no source edits, no runtime tests, no production calls, no remote writes

common_transport.statement: All listed tRPC namespaces are composed into appRouter and mounted at /api/trpc; same-origin browser transport includes credentials. Each individual procedure/service still needs its own authority and capability checks.

evidence_limits: Prior reported test success is not independently rerun by this baseline audit and does not prove universal UI coverage.
A source-connected path is not an executed production acceptance test.
Browser route fulfill can test UI recovery while bypassing the route; route.fetch then abort tests lost committed response against the real route.
Loopback payment provider proves local application integration, not live provider/card acceptance.
Fixtures often create users/permissions/bookings through API/SQL; this does not establish an admin UI for those setup steps.

findings.title: Super-admin can open the refund dashboard but its core APIs reject that role
findings.impact: The route allows admin and super_admin, but cash statistics/history/trends and split-refund queue use a local guard accepting only admin. The page renders errors for a supported platform administrator. Related refund service guards also exclude super_admin, so changing only the route guard would leave service-level failures.
findings.recommendation: Align refund platform-admin guards with existing isAdmin semantics across router and service authorization; preserve owner and tenant checks and keep ordinary user/finance roles out of platform-wide operations.
findings.minimal_acceptance: With a real super_admin session, open /admin/refunds and assert successful native statistics/history/trends/queue reads; then assert an ordinary user and finance cannot call those platform endpoints. Include an actual service-level split queue/read and a scoped forbidden target.

findings.title: Booking SMS opt-in and phone field have no persistence or notification command
findings.impact: The booking screen promises SMS booking updates and accepts an editable phone number, but both submission paths omit the fields and make no preferences or SMS call. The only integrated user SMS API reads logs/preferences; sending is administrative. The check-in reminder job explicitly defers SMS integration.
findings.recommendation: Remove or honestly disable the per-booking SMS controls until a per-booking consent/delivery contract exists. Do not silently mutate global profile preferences or trigger new paid messages. A configured Twilio provider alone does not connect booking events to SMS.
findings.minimal_acceptance: Open a real booking page and complete an existing booking path. Assert the unsupported SMS opt-in/phone field and delivery promise are absent or explicitly unavailable, no profile-preference write or SMS send is issued, and the booking still reaches its server invoice.

findings.title: Check-in reminder deep link uses an ignored parameter and a different identifier
findings.impact: The job emails /check-in?booking=<bookingReference>. CheckIn only initializes from window.history.state.checkInPnr, then calls getByPNR. bookingReference and pnr are independently generated. The CTA opens an empty search rather than selecting the intended reservation; manually entering the PNR remains possible.
findings.recommendation: Define one deliberate owner-authenticated handoff contract for emailed check-in navigation and use the same identifier on producer and consumer. Keep the already working MyBookings state handoff; avoid exposing a PNR in the URL merely to prefill. Preserve a safe return path through login.
findings.minimal_acceptance: Generate the job link from a fixture whose bookingReference differs from pnr, open it in an authenticated owner browser and verify the intended reservation; verify logged-out return-to behavior, foreign owner rejection, and no check-in mutation until explicit user action.

findings.title: Collected-but-unsettled payment recovery exists only as an API workflow
findings.impact: payments.settlementReviews and refundSettlementReview are mounted admin-only endpoints backed by payment_receipts and an idempotent provider refund. There are no client references. The refund dashboard covers cash history, internal-credit returns and split cancellation; an operator cannot inspect or execute this distinct recovery workflow through the UI. This is missing UI coverage, not an unmounted service or a claim that current production has such receipts.
findings.negative_evidence_search: rg -n settlementReviews|refundSettlementReview client/src returned no matches at the audited SHA
findings.recommendation: Provide a narrowly scoped platform-admin review panel on the existing refund/operations surface, or explicitly document API-only operations if that is the product decision. Display awaiting_webhook separately from refunded; retain the stable provider idempotency key and verified webhook authority.
findings.minimal_acceptance: Use disposable DB and the owned loopback payment provider to produce one review_required receipt; read it via the actual UI, request recovery once, retry without a duplicate provider refund, and assert awaiting_webhook before the signed event and refunded afterwards. No external payment calls.

findings.title: Bag-return capability depends on an API-only staff/station grant
findings.impact: DcsDesk renders ReturnBag only when getDesk.canReturnBags is true. That value comes from a staff/carrier/origin-station grant. setBagReturnGrant is mounted and authorized for airline administration, but client code has no call to grant or revoke it. The native desk fixture provisions the grant directly through RPC before opening the browser screen. Operator handover is connected after provisioning; the full administrator provisioning journey is absent from UI.
findings.negative_evidence_search: rg -n setBagReturnGrant client/src returned no matches at the audited SHA
findings.recommendation: Expose controlled grant/revoke administration if airline staff are expected to provision permissions entirely through UI; otherwise retain the documented API provisioning requirement. Do not automatically grant all ops users bag handover authority.
findings.minimal_acceptance: With two airline tenants, grant through the actual admin interface, verify ReturnBag becomes available only for the intended staff/carrier/station, revoke and verify immediate server rejection even if an old page remains open.

findings.title: Legacy test names overstate their assertions, but they are outside the selected required journey gate
findings.impact: booking-flow payment failure has an empty test body; admin refund processing ends expect(true). CI explicitly selects stronger modern journey files, so this does not invalidate the previously reported selected E2E gate. Do not cite those legacy names as integration evidence.
findings.recommendation: Treat legacy tests as non-evidence; replace only when their uncovered behavior becomes an intended acceptance gate. Avoid rerunning broad suites just to improve the count.

journeys.action: Admin inspects persisted observations, acknowledges alert and retries eligible events/cancellations

not_confirmed_as_gaps: Scoped finance components are also reachable at /airline; platform AdminRoute on revenue-accounting is not proof finance lacks those tools.
Payment provider selector being unused does not itself prove a gap: the booking checkout backend deliberately supports Stripe settlement only.
Training/demo/APIS unavailable screens are not successful production integrations and should not be enabled merely for UI completeness.
